## Grammar

Basic word order is SOV; it has postpositions. In the noun phrase: possessor before the possessed; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; noun before the numeral; relative clause before the noun. Overall it is head-final.
It has no definite article, no indefinite article, a rich case system, ergative-absolutive alignment, no grammatical number, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past, future and perfective; there is an indirect (reported or inferred) evidential. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs agree with the subject by suffixes; not with the object.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; verb reduplication; a copula; a bound causative; a bound passive; question words moved to the front; a decimal counting base; a 'have' verb for possession.
Measured morphology: 1 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 1.0 (0 free word … 3 fused), 0 paradigm cells, 0 of them with allomorphy.
